---
title: "CanadaLogin Signal Check"
subtitle: "For the two-week period of October 19 to November 1"
author: "EDCP Data and Research Team"  # colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca
date: "2026-11-02"
params:
  edition: 10
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    theme: [cosmo, _fonts.scss]   # _fonts.scss: self-hosted brand fonts
    toc: false
    fig-width: 8
    fig-height: 3.4
execute:

---

```{r setup}
# Queries are frozen to the October 19 - November 1, 2026 period.
source("../R/connection.R")
source("../R/branding.R")
source("../R/colours.R")
source("../R/publishing.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(dbplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
})

con <- connect_athena()

# Watermark date: the date this report is first created.
report_date <- as.Date("2026-11-02")

period_start <- as.Date("2026-10-19")
period_end <- as.Date("2026-11-01")

# Google Analytics is exported on a two-day lag, so its view ends a day early.
ga_period_end <- as.Date("2026-10-31")

# Monday of the launch week; the service went live Apr 22.
series_start <- as.Date("2026-04-20")

# The first month boundary after launch, where figure 1's axis labels start.
first_month_break <- as.Date("2026-05-01")

# Daily share of monthly users: whole calendar months only.
share_start <- as.Date("2026-05-01")
share_end <- as.Date("2026-10-31")

prev_end <- period_start - 1

# Public relying parties from the rp schema, one row per application name.
relying_parties <- load_relying_parties(con) |>
  filter(!is_internal)

# Figure 1 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Public services and the departments and agencies behind them, by registry
# launch date. A department counts once, from its first service.
public_services <- distinct(
  relying_parties, service_name, operator, gc_orgid, launch_date
)

partners_on <- function(d) {
  live <- public_services[public_services$launch_date <= d, ]
  c(services = nrow(live), departments = n_distinct(live$gc_orgid))
}

partner_growth <- tibble(day = seq(series_start, period_end, by = "day")) |>
  mutate(
    services = vapply(day, \(d) partners_on(d)[["services"]], integer(1)),
    departments = vapply(day, \(d) partners_on(d)[["departments"]], integer(1))
  )

partners_now <- partners_on(period_end)

newcomers <- public_services |>
  filter(launch_date >= period_start, launch_date <= period_end) |>
  arrange(launch_date)

# Users by first day, from the event stream. The day comes from the time string
# because this role cannot filter partitions; "UNKNOWN" has no account.
stream_daily <- tbl(
  con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "authentication_activity")
) |>
  filter(!is.na(subject), subject != "", subject != "UNKNOWN") |>
  group_by(subject) |>
  summarise(first_day = min(substr(time, 1L, 10L)), .groups = "drop") |>
  count(first_day, name = "new_users") |>
  collect() |>
  transmute(day = as.Date(first_day), new_users = as.double(new_users)) |>
  arrange(day) |>
  mutate(users = cumsum(new_users)) |>
  filter(day <= period_end)

stream_total <- max(stream_daily$users)
new_this_period <- stream_total -
  max(stream_daily$users[stream_daily$day <= prev_end])

# Figure 2 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Migration task success, new-account funnel: the stored 7-day and daily
# rates, never recomputed.
migration_funnel <- "migration_new_to_cl"

migration_rates <- tbl(
  con, in_schema("google_analytics", "funnel_metrics_current")
) |>
  filter(
    funnel_id == migration_funnel,
    metric_id == "task_success",
    window_days %in% c("1", "7"),
    breakdown_value == "RESERVED_TOTAL",
    !window_incomplete
  ) |>
  select(window_days, window_end, funnel_version, value) |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(window_end = as.Date(window_end)) |>
  filter(window_end <= ga_period_end)

# Starters are the rate's denominator, users who did not skip the prompt.
migration_starters <- tbl(
  con, in_schema("google_analytics", "funnels_current")
) |>
  filter(
    funnel_id == migration_funnel,
    window_days == "1",
    breakdown_value == "RESERVED_TOTAL",
    funnelstepname == "migration_not_skipped",
    !window_incomplete
  ) |>
  select(window_end, starters = activeusers) |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(window_end = as.Date(window_end), starters = as.double(starters)) |>
  filter(window_end <= ga_period_end)

migration_daily <- migration_rates |>
  filter(window_days == "1") |>
  inner_join(migration_starters, by = "window_end")

migration_weekly <- filter(migration_rates, window_days == "7") |>
  arrange(window_end)

# The first full Monday-Sunday week, read at its Sunday.
migration_first <- migration_weekly |>
  filter(format(window_end, "%u") == "7") |>
  slice_min(window_end, n = 1)
migration_latest <- slice_max(migration_weekly, window_end, n = 1)

# ATIP's share of the latest week's starters. ATIP traffic had no service name
# in Google Analytics until October 20, so earlier weeks undercount it.
atip_starters <- tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "funnels_current")) |>
  filter(
    funnel_id == migration_funnel,
    window_days == "7",
    funnelstepname == "migration_not_skipped",
    !window_incomplete,
    as.Date(window_end) == ga_period_end
  ) |>
  select(breakdown_value, starters = activeusers) |>
  collect()

# Google Analytics names the Request Service by its long form.
is_atip <- startsWith(atip_starters$breakdown_value, "Access to Information") |
  startsWith(atip_starters$breakdown_value, "ATIP")
atip_share <- sum(atip_starters$starters[is_atip]) /
  atip_starters$starters[atip_starters$breakdown_value == "RESERVED_TOTAL"]

# ATIP's two services joined on the same day.
atip_launch <- min(
  relying_parties$launch_date[startsWith(relying_parties$service_name, "ATIP")]
)

# Figure 3 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Daily share of monthly users (DAU/MAU) per application and calendar month,
# per the cookbook's daily-share-of-monthly-users recipe.
app_logins <- tbl(
  con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_transformed", "events_app_login_counts")
)

first_seen <- app_logins |>
  group_by(application_name) |>
  summarise(first_day = min(as.Date(from_date), na.rm = TRUE))

services <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  select(application_name = alias, service_name_en, is_internal)

monthly_share <- app_logins |>
  # whole, finished calendar months only
  filter(
    as.Date(from_date) >= share_start,
    as.Date(from_date) <= share_end
  ) |>
  group_by(
    application_name, month = floor_date(as.Date(from_date), "month")
  ) |>
  summarise(
    user_days = sum(unique_users, na.rm = TRUE),
    # mtd_unique_users only grows within a month, so its maximum is the
    # month's distinct users even when the last day has no row
    monthly_active_users = max(mtd_unique_users, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  inner_join(first_seen, by = "application_name") |>
  # live for the whole month: first row before the 1st
  filter(first_day < month) |>
  # a left join keeps an application with no alias row
  left_join(services, by = "application_name") |>
  filter(!coalesce(is_internal, FALSE)) |>
  mutate(
    days_in_month = day(last_day_of_month(month)),
    dau_mau_ratio = as.double(user_days) / days_in_month /
      monthly_active_users,
    active_days_per_user = as.double(user_days) / monthly_active_users
  ) |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(month = as.Date(month))

latest_month <- max(monthly_share$month)

# The two ATIP services sit at opposite ends, so their rows name who uses them.
audience_tags <- c(
  "ATIP Online Management Tools" = "staff",
  "ATIP Online Request Service" = "public"
)

# One row per application in the latest month. MyCGC runs on two platforms,
# so its rows name the platform.
share_labels <- monthly_share |>
  filter(month == latest_month) |>
  add_count(service_name_en, name = "apps_in_service") |>
  transmute(application_name, label = case_when(
    apps_in_service > 1 ~ paste0(
      service_name_en, " (",
      sub(".*CGC - (.*) - Prod$", "\\1", application_name), ")"
    ),
    service_name_en %in% names(audience_tags) ~ paste0(
      service_name_en, " (", audience_tags[service_name_en], ")"
    ),
    .default = service_name_en
  ))

monthly_share <- inner_join(
  monthly_share, share_labels, by = "application_name"
)
share_latest <- filter(monthly_share, month == latest_month)
share_earlier <- filter(monthly_share, month < latest_month)

share_top <- slice_max(share_latest, dau_mau_ratio, n = 1)
share_bottom <- slice_min(share_latest, dau_mau_ratio, n = 1)

# Every user signing in on exactly one day of the month.
share_floor <- 1 / unique(share_latest$days_in_month)
```

This is the **CanadaLogin Signal Check**, where we tell you what's
interesting in CanadaLogin reporting this week. This edition covers three things: the services and departments now
using CanadaLogin, how to keep up to date with task success metrics, and how
frequently a user of a given online service signs in.

**CanadaLogin now serves `r partners_now[["services"]]` public services from
`r partners_now[["departments"]]` departments and agencies.** Two services
joined in the last two weeks: the `r newcomers$service_name[1]` on
`r format_long_date(newcomers$launch_date[1])` and
`r newcomers$service_name[2]` on
`r format_long_date(newcomers$launch_date[2])`. Both are just starting,
with only a handful of users so far. Users kept growing too: CanadaLogin had
**`r comma(stream_total)`** users since launch by
`r format_long_date(period_end)`, and **`r comma(new_this_period)`** of them
joined in the last two weeks.

```{r partner-growth}
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Step chart from April to November 1, 2026, of public services on
#|   CanadaLogin (blue) and the departments and agencies behind them (green).
#|   Both start at 1 in April. By November 1 there are 11 services from 9
#|   departments and agencies, with two services added in the last two weeks.
partner_long <- partner_growth |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(services, departments), names_to = "measure") |>
  # Departments draw last, so the green line shows where the two overlap.
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, c("services", "departments")))

partner_colours <- c(
  services = unname(colors$brand["blue"]),
  departments = unname(colors$brand["green"])
)
partner_labels <- c(
  services = "public services",
  departments = "departments and agencies"
)

partner_ends <- filter(partner_long, day == period_end) |>
  mutate(label = paste(value, partner_labels[measure]))

partner_plot <- ggplot(partner_long, aes(day, value, colour = measure)) +
  annotate(
    "rect", xmin = period_start, xmax = period_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = colors$greyscale[5]
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = period_start - 2, y = 1, hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 3,
    colour = "grey30", lineheight = 0.9,
    label = paste0("New this period:\n", paste(newcomers$service_name,
                                               collapse = "\n"))
  ) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = partner_ends, size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(
    data = partner_ends, aes(label = label), hjust = 1, vjust = -0.9,
    fontface = "bold", size = 3.4
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = partner_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA), breaks = seq(0, 12, by = 2),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  # Monthly, not weekly: the counts change a few times a season.
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(first_month_break, period_end, by = "month"),
    date_labels = "%b", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.01))
  ) +
  theme_cds() +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "On CanadaLogin",
    title = "More services, and more departments, are joining CanadaLogin",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Public services and the departments and agencies that run them, by ",
      "launch date."
    )
  )

add_cds_logo(add_watermark(partner_plot, date = report_date,
                           edition = params$edition))
```

**You can track task success in the Experience Monitoring dashboard.** The
Task Success Report, previously published every month, will now be shared
when there is something noteworthy to report. For regular updates, EDCP
employees can check the [Experience Monitoring
dashboard](`r published_url("experience-monitoring.html")`), which tracks
task success for each task and is updated weekly, on Tuesdays. Our team has
used it internally until now, and we are working on updating it to make it
more user friendly.

The chart below is one of the Experience Monitoring dashboard's figures. It
shows migration: users moving an old sign-in, such as GCKey, to a new
CanadaLogin account. The violet line is the
share of users who finished over the past seven days, and each grey dot is a
single day, sized by how many users started. Migration success rose from
`r percent(migration_first$value, accuracy = 1)` in early August to
**`r percent(migration_latest$value, accuracy = 1)`** by
`r format_long_date(ga_period_end)`. Most of these users come from ATIP,
which had **`r percent(atip_share, accuracy = 1)`** of starters in the
latest week, and the jump in early September came from a few very busy
days after ATIP joined CanadaLogin.

```{r migration-task-success}
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-alt: |
#|   The Experience Monitoring dashboard's task success chart for migration to
#|   a new CanadaLogin account, August to October 31, 2026: a violet 7-day
#|   rate over grey daily points sized by starters. The rate rises from 53% in
#|   early August to 68% by October 31. A labelled arrow marks ATIP joining
#|   on September 2, when large daily points lift the line to about 84% for a
#|   week.
# Styled after the dashboard's funnel chart, so readers recognise it there.
expmon_accent <- "#4B2E83"
expmon_annotation <- "grey45"
expmon_headroom <- 0.2

# A labelled arrow points down at the 7-day line on the day ATIP joined.
atip_on_line <- approx(
  migration_weekly$window_end, migration_weekly$value, atip_launch
)$y

migration_plot <- ggplot() +
  annotate(
    "segment", x = atip_launch, xend = atip_launch,
    y = atip_on_line + 0.15, yend = atip_on_line + 0.03,
    colour = expmon_annotation, linewidth = 0.5,
    arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.06, "inches"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = atip_launch, y = atip_on_line + 0.19,
    label = paste0(
      "ATIP joins CanadaLogin, ", format(atip_launch, "%b "),
      as.integer(format(atip_launch, "%d"))
    ),
    colour = expmon_annotation, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = migration_daily, aes(window_end, value, size = starters),
    colour = "grey70", alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  scale_size(range = c(0.4, 2.4), labels = comma, name = "Starters per day") +
  # Grouped by version so the line breaks where the definition changes.
  geom_line(
    data = migration_weekly,
    aes(window_end, value, group = funnel_version),
    colour = expmon_accent, linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = migration_latest, aes(window_end, value),
    colour = expmon_accent, size = 2.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = migration_latest,
    aes(window_end, value, label = percent(value, accuracy = 1)),
    colour = expmon_accent, vjust = 2, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, expmon_headroom)), oob = oob_keep
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(monday_of(min(migration_daily$window_end)) + 6,
                 ga_period_end, by = "week"),
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  ) +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = "left"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Task success rate",
    title = "Task Success: Migration, new CanadaLogin account",
    subtitle = paste(
      "7-day rolling rate (violet line) over the daily rate (grey points).",
      "All relying parties. Rate is of users who answered the migration prompt.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  )

# Taller figure, so the logo height fraction is scaled to match the others.
add_cds_logo(
  add_watermark(migration_plot, date = report_date, edition = params$edition),
  height = 0.13 * 3.4 / 4.2
)
```

**Most users sign in on about two days a month.** A new measure, the
[daily share of monthly
users](https://cds-snc.github.io/canadalogin-metrics-cookbook/cookbook/ibm_verify/daily-share-of-monthly-users.html),
shows how frequently a user of a given online service signs in. It is the
share of a month's users who sign in on a typical day, effectively daily
active users over monthly active users (DAU/MAU). If every user signed in
on just one day a month, it would be about
`r percent(share_floor, accuracy = 1)`.

In `r format(latest_month, "%B")`, users of
`r share_top$service_name_en` signed in most often:
**`r percent(share_top$dau_mau_ratio, accuracy = 1)`** of them on a typical
day, or about `r round(share_top$active_days_per_user)` days each. Users of
the `r share_bottom$service_name_en` signed in least often:
**`r percent(share_bottom$dau_mau_ratio, accuracy = 1)`**, or about
`r round(share_bottom$active_days_per_user)` days each. Both are ATIP
services: staff who process requests use the Management Tools as part of
their job, while Canadians use the Request Service to file a request, often
just once. This measure will help us estimate support demand when large new
programs join CanadaLogin.

```{r share-of-monthly-users}
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Dot chart of the daily share of monthly users for each public
#|   application in October 2026, with earlier months as grey dots. ATIP
#|   Online Management Tools, used by staff, is highest at 15%, about 5 days a
#|   month, and ATIP Online Request Service, used by the public, is lowest at
#|   6%, about 2 days. The axis starts at 3%, the lowest possible value,
#|   where every user signs in on one day a month.
share_order <- share_latest$label[order(share_latest$dau_mau_ratio)]

# Each label sits past its row's furthest dot, so it never covers one.
share_text <- monthly_share |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(x = max(dau_mau_ratio), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(share_latest, by = "label")

share_plot <- ggplot(mapping = aes(dau_mau_ratio, label)) +
  geom_point(data = share_earlier, colour = colors$greyscale[4], size = 2) +
  geom_point(data = share_latest, colour = colors$brand["blue"], size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(
    data = share_text,
    aes(x = x, label = paste0(percent(dau_mau_ratio, accuracy = 1), " (",
                              round(active_days_per_user, 1), " days)")),
    hjust = -0.2, size = 3.2
  ) +
  # Starts at the floor, not zero: no application can score below it.
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1),
    breaks = c(share_floor, seq(0.05, 0.15, by = 0.05)),
    limits = c(share_floor, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))
  ) +
  # Fixed order: layers would otherwise set it by which draws first.
  scale_y_discrete(limits = share_order) +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) +
  labs(
    x = "Daily share of monthly users", y = NULL,
    title = "Users of work tools and repeat services sign in most often",
    subtitle = paste0(
      format(latest_month, "%B %Y"), " (blue, days per user) and earlier ",
      "months (grey)."
    )
  )

# Taller figure, so the logo height fraction is scaled to match the others.
add_cds_logo(
  add_watermark(share_plot, date = report_date, edition = params$edition),
  height = 0.13 * 3.4 / 4.2
)
```
